jobs.title: PhD Position in Data-driven Critical Raw Material Supply Chain Resilience
jobs.description:
Do you want to investigate the resilience of critical raw material supply chains supporting low-carbon and digital technologies? Join us as a PhD student at SDU Life Cycle Engineering, University of Southern Denmark.

The Department of Green Technology at the University of Southern Denmark invites applications for a three-year PhD position in data-driven critical raw material supply chain resilience.

The position will be based at SDU Life Cycle Engineering, Department of Green Technology, Faculty of Engineering, at the SDU Odense campus. The expected starting date is 15 February 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

 

Project Overview

The deployment of low-carbon technologies, electrification and digital infrastructure is increasing global demand for critical raw materials. At the same time, the production and processing of many of these materials are geographically concentrated and exposed to geopolitical, economic, environmental and logistical disruptions.

Understanding how technology development affects material demand, in-use stocks, end-of-life flows and global supply dependencies is therefore important for assessing and strengthening the resilience of critical raw material supply chains.

The PhD position is jointly funded through research projects on critical raw material supply chains and material requirements for Denmark’s climate-neutral transition. The project will be embedded in an interdisciplinary research environment combining environmental systems analysis, supply-chain research and data science.

 

PhD Topic Description

The PhD project will develop modular and data-driven approaches for analysing critical raw material demand, supply-chain dependencies and resilience.

A central methodological contribution will be the development of transparent, reusable and reproducible computational modules for dynamic material flow analysis. The modules will support the integration of technology deployment scenarios, material intensities, product lifetimes, stocks and flows, end-of-life management, recycling, production, trade, facility and ownership data.

The developed approaches will be applied to selected technology systems, including Denmark’s wind-energy infrastructure and the rapidly expanding infrastructure supporting data centres and AI computing. These cases will be analysed within a common methodological framework to examine how infrastructure expansion and technological change influence demand for critical and scarce materials, in-use stocks, future waste flows, recycling potential and global supply-chain dependencies.

The project may also investigate overlapping material requirements and competition for materials across low-carbon and digital technologies. Particular attention may be given to supply concentration, host–by-product dependencies, trade and ownership structures, supply bottlenecks, cascading risks and potential resilience strategies.

Depending on the candidate’s academic background and the specific research questions, the project may include network analysis, geospatial analysis, scenario modelling, uncertainty analysis, machine learning and other AI-supported approaches.

The candidate will build on selected existing models, datasets and research activities in the group and further develop scientifically robust and reusable methods that improve transparency, comparability and reproducibility in material-system research.

The exact research focus and detailed PhD plan will be developed jointly with the successful candidate, taking into account the project objectives, academic background and research interests.

In addition to a PhD dissertation and high-quality scientific publications, the project is expected to produce reusable modelling methods, documented datasets and reproducible computational workflows.

 

PhD Position and Research Environment

As a PhD student, you will conduct independent research under the supervision of an interdisciplinary team, contribute to high-quality scientific publications and participate actively in a collaborative research environment.

You will join SDU Life Cycle Engineering, where research covers industrial ecology, material flow analysis, life cycle assessment, circular economy, resource systems and sustainability transitions.

The project connects expertise in engineering, data science, mathematics, business, supply-chain research and geological resources. The wider research environment includes competences in material flow analysis, critical raw material systems, data mining, network analysis, supply-chain science, finance, investment, ownership structures, geological resources and technology systems.

The position provides opportunities for collaboration across SDU faculties and with external research partners. It may also include participation in international conferences, research visits and collaboration with relevant industrial and public-sector stakeholders.

The PhD programme follows the Danish PhD framework and includes coursework, participation in active research environments, dissemination activities, and teaching or other knowledge-dissemination duties.

 

What We Expect

We are looking for a highly motivated, independent and collaborative candidate with a strong interest in critical raw materials, quantitative modelling, data-driven research and sustainability.

Applicants must hold a relevant master’s degree or equivalent by the time of enrolment. Relevant academic backgrounds may include engineering, industrial ecology, sustainability science, resource management, data science, computer science, applied mathematics, operations research, supply-chain management, geoinformatics, mining or geological sciences, or another relevant natural science or quantitative discipline.

The successful candidate should demonstrate:

  • A solid academic foundation in quantitative analysis, system modelling, data science or related methods. 

  • Experience with programming and data analysis, preferably using Python or a similar programming language. 

  • Experience with data handling, including data cleaning, transformation, integration and exploratory analysis. 

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. 

  • The ability to work independently and collaboratively in an interdisciplinary research environment. 

  • Good written and spoken English. 

  • A strong interest in sustainability, critical raw materials and supply-chain resilience. 

Experience in one or more of the following areas will be considered an advantage:

  • Material flow analysis, industrial ecology or material systems modelling. 

  • Network, supply-chain or geospatial analysis. 

  • Scientific computing and reproducible research workflows. 

  • Statistics, machine learning, artificial intelligence, optimisation, uncertainty or scenario analysis. 

  • International trade, production facility or corporate ownership data. 

  • Critical raw materials, wind energy, digital infrastructure or data centres. 

Applicants are not expected to possess expertise in all these areas. Prior experience with material flow analysis is an advantage but is not a requirement. Relevant training will be provided according to the candidate’s background and the needs of the project.

 

Application

Before applying the candidates are advised to read the Faculty information for prospective PhD students and the SDU information on how to apply.

The application must be submitted in English through the SDU online recruitment system.

Assessment of applicants will be based on the submitted application material. The application must include:

  • Curriculum Vitae. 

  • A motivated application describing the applicant’s research interests, relevant qualifications and motivation for applying. 

  • Documentation of academic qualifications, including bachelor’s and master’s degree certificates and complete transcripts of grades. 

  • Official English translations of documents not issued in English or Danish. 

  • Two letters of recommendation. 

  • A list of publications and up to two examples of relevant publications, if available. 

  • The completed TEK PhD application form for 5+3 applicants. Find the form at the Faculty website.

  • The completed TEK form for calculation of grade-point average. Find the form at the Faculty website.

  • Official documentation describing the grading system of the awarding university, if the degree was not obtained in Denmark. 

  • Examples of relevant thesis work, software, code repositories or other research outputs, where available. 

  • Only for applicants from programmes that evaluate thesis/examination project by approved/not approved: An official written assessment of the thesis or dissertation project from the grade giving institution. The statement must clearly state that the candidate has been among the top 30 pct. in the graduation class for the study programme.

All documents must be in English and PDF format. CPR number (civil registration number) must be crossed out. All PDF-files must be unlocked, allow binding and may not be password protected. 

SUBMISSION GUIDE: Motivated application must be uploaded under ‘Cover letter’ (max. 5 MB), Curriculum Vitae must be uploaded under ‘Resume’ (max 5 MB). All other documents must be uploaded under ‘Miscellaneous documents’ (max 10 files with a maximum 50 MB per file). 

For administrative questions regarding the recruitment process, please contact our email support.

 

The application deadline is November 15, 2026, at 11:59 PM/23:59 (CET/CEST) 

 

Enrollment and employment terms

Appointment as a PhD fellow is a 3-year salaried position, and the monthly gross salary incl. pension is 37.075 DKK. If you have relevant postgraduate experience, you may be placed on a higher salary step. The place of employment is in Odense, Denmark and preferred starting date is February 15, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

Applicants must hold a master’s degree (equivalent to a Danish master's degree) at the time of enrollment and employment. Employment is contingent on enrollment approved by the PhD School. Enrollment will be in accordance with Faculty regulations and the Danish Ministerial Order on the PhD Programme at the Universities (PhD order). Employment will be in accordance with the collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations for academics in the state including the associated circular on the job structure for academic staff at Danish universities and the provisions for PhD fellows as described therein as well as the Protocol on PhD fellows signed by the Danish Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC). 

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements. As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process. SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary. Further information on salary and taxation. 

Persons employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a “self-organizer”.

-

The University of Southern Denmark wishes its staff to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. SDU conducts research in critical technologies, which, due to the risk of unwanted knowledge transfer, is subject to a number of security measures. Therefore, based on information from open sources, background checks may be conducted on candidates for the position(s).

 

SDU Life Cycle Engineering

The successful candidate will be affiliated with SDU Life Cycle Engineering at the Department of Green Technology. The research environment conducts interdisciplinary research on the global and systemic interactions between materials, technologies, energy, the environment and society.

The Department of Green Technology is located in Odense, the main campus of the University of Southern Denmark. Odense offers an international research environment and an open Scandinavian working culture.

 

Further Information

Associate Professor
Department of Green Technology
SDU Life Cycle Engineering

jobs.title: Natural Hazards Mission Lead
jobs.description:
ETH Zurich is establishing the ETH Swiss GeoLab, a new interdisciplinary unit of ETH Zürich I Space. ETH Space will soon become one of few strategic centres of ETH Zurich, and encompasses overall five units.

The GeoLab is focused on Earth observation and its applications. The GeoLab uses satellite, airborne, ground-based and in-situ observations. To these diverse data sets it applies AI-driven analysis methods and high-performance computing to develop solutions for specific societal and economic challenges.

Located at the D4 Business Village in Root, close to Lucerne, ETH Swiss GeoLab works at the interface of research, technology development and practical application. In its first phase, the GeoLab is focusing on few selected high-impact application areas where Earth observation, geodata and AI-based analytics can create tangible value for Switzerland. The Natural Hazards Mission focuses initially on mass movements, including landslides and rockfalls, with the aim of improving early detection, monitoring, preparedness and decision support for Swiss practitioners, authorities and infrastructure stakeholders. It builds on stakeholder engagement, solution scoping and community-building activities already underway within GeoLab, including contributions from senior domain experts and partners in the Swiss natural hazards community.

The ETH Swiss GeoLab is led by Prof. Dr Verena Griess and Prof. Dr Thomas Zurbuchen, with Dr Felix Seidel as Managing Director, responsible for the day-to-day operations of this exciting activity. The GeoLab will grow into a project-based hub of around 100 experts over the coming years and will collaborate closely with other ETH units, the Swiss National Supercomputing Centre (CSCS), Swiss research institutions, public-sector stakeholders, natural hazard organisations, industry partners, start-ups and international stakeholders.

This position is offered as a fixed-term appointment for an initial period of two years, with the possibility of extension.

As Natural Hazards Mission Lead, you will lead the research and development portfolio, integration and delivery of GeoLab’s Natural Hazards Mission. Initially focused on landslides and rockfalls, and later expanding to other natural hazards, you will help define the mission vision, translate user needs into research and product requirements, and ensure that GeoLab activities create measurable value for Swiss practice and public decision-making. You will build on ongoing interchange with key stakeholders and solution-scoping activities already underway within GeoLab, and work closely with senior domain-relevant partners, technical teams and experts.

You will report to the Managing Director of ETH Swiss GeoLab and work closely with GeoLab’s Natural Hazards Community & Solutions Lead, other GeoLab mission teams, the Research Program Support team, and the Geo-Intelligence team and external partners. You will define priorities, milestones and decision points, lead mission delivery and will have the authority to prioritize, redirect, and pivot or pause activities within your research and development portfolio, the approved mission charter, budget and governance framework.

As part of your role, you will:

On behalf of the GeoLab leadership team, define an ambitious and coherent research and development portfolio for the Natural Hazards Mission, initially centred on landslides and rockfalls
Translate identified critical operational gaps into measurable outcomes that create value for practitioners, authorities and decision-makers
Engage with local, cantonal and federal authorities, infrastructure operators, practitioners, industry and expert communities, in coordination with GeoLab leadership and existing Natural Hazards community activities
Translate operational challenges into research, data, product and technical requirements
Establish measurable mission outcomes, roadmaps, assumptions and success criteria aligned with Swiss natural hazard needs and the overall GeoLab strategy; you will also track progress actively against these outcomes
Manage the delegated mission budget and define priorities, milestones, decision points and success criteria and track finances and successes in that framework, through regular reporting activities to GeoLab leadership and other stakeholders
Work with the Geo-Lab’s Intelligence team – the team deeply focused on AI and Earth  observation foundational models - and external performers to drive pilots, field validation, operational testing and integration into user workflows
Assess evidence and performance, and recommend continuation, redirection, scaling, pausing or termination of activities
Identify and mobilise strong ETH groups, research institutions, engineering and geology offices, remote-sensing companies, public agencies and implementation partners
Represent ETH Swiss GeoLab in Swiss natural hazard, scientific, policy and industry communities, in coordination with GeoLab leadership and existing Natural Hazards community activities
Communicate mission goals, progress, evidence and lessons learned to internal and external stakeholders
Guide and train students, researchers and external contributors where required and support the transfer of resulting capabilities into operational practice
In summary, you understand the needs of practitioners and decision-makers in the field of natural hazards and their relation to Earth observations from space and are motivated by the opportunity to translate research and technology into practical solutions with measurable impact.

Specifically, we are looking for someone with:

A Master’s or PhD degree (preferred) in natural hazards, geosciences, engineering, risk management or related fields
Several years of experience in natural hazard practice, applied research, public administration, consulting, engineering or industry, preferably but not necessarily in Switzerland
Strong expertise and understanding of natural hazards with demonstrated examples of dashboard and tracking tools for others to gain insights in these projects
Proven ability to identify important operational problems and translate them into actionable initiatives
With a track-record of successful collaborations in diverse teams and have demonstrated your excitement to not only do research but apply that research to the benefit of others.
Experience in mission, programme or applied R&D portfolio design
Strong project, portfolio and budget management skills with demonstrated examples of transparent reporting, dashboard and tracking tools for others to gain insights in these projects
Excellent stakeholder management skills across diverse public authorities, academia, industry and expert communities
The ability to work across disciplinary and organisational boundaries and to lead through influence
Strong judgement skills under uncertainty and the willingness to challenge established approaches constructively
Excellent communication and listening skills, and great presentation skills in various modalities
Excellent written and spoken English and German; French is an asset
You are mission-driven, entrepreneurial, a strong learner and comfortable working in a newly established and evolving organisation. You have a track-record of successful team participation and leadership and an excitement for hard and impactful work. You combine scientific credibility with pragmatic decision-making, economic awareness and a clear focus on adoption, operational relevance and measurable value. In doing so, you want to work on the best idea, not necessarily your best idea.

A rare opportunity to help build ETH Swiss GeoLab from its early phase and shape a new national initiative for Earth observation
A mission-driven role with high visibility and strong societal relevance
The opportunity to develop solutions for pressing natural hazard challenges in Switzerland, and with broad international impact through transferable methods and lessons learned
A workplace in Root/Lucerne, embedded in an active innovation ecosystem and closely connected to ETH Zurich

Your CV
Diplomas and work certificates

A video (max 2 mins) about you and your motivation for this position

- Collaborate with medical and evidence generation / HEOR teams to identify evidence gaps and integrate timely access needs within the evidence strategy, ensuring new clinical data and RWE strengthens payer value narratives (contributing to business cases to support prioritization of evidence generation as needed).

Future Readiness / capability
- Monitor and interpret market access trends, reimbursement policy changes, and coverage decisions; identify payer evidence gaps; and translate insights into actions on emerging opportunities and risks, in partnership with GPA access strategy and pipeline teams.
- Lead a multi‑layer TA Access function across the IBU to ensure cross‑market consistency, execution excellence, share practices and accelerated access outcomes; define TA‑specific capabilities and implement the agreed operating model in partnership with Global Access, Global Pricing, IBU Medical, MCE, and IBU Regulatory.
- Equip, guide and train local teams/partners with processes, standards, tools, and decision frameworks to build high-quality LOCs access excellence in execution.
-Lead and be a role model to digital capability adoption throughout the access community
- Develop and run mock negotiations within the specific TA and orchestrate capability training, and simulation exercises for markets.
- Foster collaboration and best practice sharing across GPA teams, access and cross-functions and geographies partners.
- Lead and contribute to strategic initiatives sponsored by the GPA function or Takeda, broadening organizational impact, strengthening cross-functional alignment, and driving enterprise value (mAI access – CXF – JHTA – VBHC ...)

Skills:
- Solid experience in Local and preferably Regional Market Access & Pricing, with demonstrated leadership across TA areas and complex payer environments.
- Proven ability to shape TA‑level access strategy across the full asset lifecycle (launch, inline, LOE), including advisory to senior governance bodies.
- Deep knowledge of global payer systems, reimbursement pathways and pricing dynamics, particularly across Europe and Intercontinental markets.
- Strong portfolio readiness expertise, including payer scenario planning, pricing insights & trends, evidence requirements, and competitive access risk management.
- Advanced capability to integrate clinical, HEOR, RWE and competitive insights into clear payer value propositions and access decision‑making.
- Demonstrated matrix leadership, working effectively with Global Access, Pricing, Medical, Regulatory and Commercial partners and being at ease to navigate a complex matrix of multi stakeholders.
- Project/program management and prioritization capability across parallel workstreams and deadlines.
- People and capability cross-functional influencing experience, including leading multi‑layer, geographically dispersed Access teams and driving functional capability development.
- Learning agility to adapt to new assets within the assigned TA, portfolio or any new situation, continuing to lead within changes and uncertainties and deliver results.
- Strategic thinking: Ability to think strategically and make sound, forward-looking decisions, based on strong business acumen to identify challenges and opportunities and drive impact.
- Communication: Ability to communicate effectively and influence diverse global and Local stakeholders with strong interpersonal and influencing skills in a multicultural, international environment and proven ability to build alignment.
- Resilience with ambiguity and cross-cultural collaboration across international markets/partners.
- Digital and AI-forward: Experience leveraging digital platforms, data analytics, and AI-driven tools to enhance decision-making and access strategy execution is a plus

jobs.description:
At Syngenta Group, we're a global community of 56,000 innovators across 90 countries, united by a 250-year legacy of agricultural excellence. As the world's most local agricultural technology partner, we create tailor-made solutions that transform farming while protecting our planet, driven by our commitment to innovation, ethics, and integrity. Through our inclusive environment and diverse perspectives, we pioneer breakthrough solutions for farmers, society, and future generations. Join our worldwide teams of agricultural pioneers in creating a more resilient and equitable food system for all.

Purpose
•    Provide technical leadership for a particular product or capability within the Process Technology (PT) environment, holding the chemistry and process know-how for assigned chemical steps.
•    Lead the local technical team in the development, introduction, and support of chemical processes for new and mature intermediates and/or active substances, in close collaboration with WMU and Global Process Technology.
•    Drive improvement plans for chemical processes to increase capacity, improve quality, and reduce costs, while troubleshooting process issues (leading cost and process learning curves).
•    Support process relocation projects to external suppliers or other manufacturing sites, and coach junior chemists.

Accountabilities

General & HSE:
•    Ensure that the manufacturing process is safe and compliant with legal and internal HSE rules at all times.
•    Ensure process design meets the requirements of company and national HSEQ and regulatory standards (e.g., Chemical Reaction Hazards, PRA, Management of Change).
•    Define, plan, and control laboratory work, semi-technical, and full-scale plant trials to develop and test new or improved manufacturing processes.
•    Lead programs of scientific work, defining individual tasks and technical designs within complex, challenging projects.
•    Store project data electronically and compile technical reports to record and share experimental results.
•    Actively participate in local and global technical networks to share knowledge and stay connected with other Syngenta sites (CHMU, GBJH, etc.).
Production Support:
•    Define key process parameters and design control strategies to ensure they remain within safe and optimal limits.
•    Provide proactive technical support and troubleshooting to manufacturing plants to restore or improve production performance.
•    Deliver technological recommendations to improve plant capacity, production costs, waste reduction, and energy consumption.
Supply Chain & Project Support:
•    Understand supply chain requirements and take a leading role in delivering objectives (acting as the Technology Lead for specific Active Ingredients (AIs) when required).

•    Responsible and varied work in a forward-thinking company

jobs.description:

Responsible for execution of Gasoline Blending operations and trader support. The role co-ordinates all aspects of post-deal trading activity to ensure contract execution runs efficiently, provides commercial and market information to the trader as necessary, and reviews and comments on contracts and tenders to ensure consistency with the trade ticket and recap.

For all Gasoline blended cargoes, be the key point of contact between the commercial desk and external stakeholders.
Liaise with terminals and vessels to ensure commercial blending plans are followed in line with the traders’ expectations.
Ensure with inspection companies that quality is as per blend plans and in line with contractual provisions.
Investigate Quantity losses and explore remedial action.
Trouble shoot when plans change and provide solutions.
Actively manage the terminals line up to mitigate demurrage.
Review stowage plans and monitor vessel progress during voyages.
Appoint third-party providers in line with group policy; oversee clean acceptance of vessels on subjects and chartering progress.
Liaise and co-ordinate with Finance, providing accurate and timely data needed for the issuance of L/Cs and P/Us.
Issue documentary instructions to suppliers and handle all aspects of customs exportation/importation where applicable.
Maintain good contract and shipping files electronically; keep Pluto updated regularly and minimise exceptions.
Complete voyage and storage reconciliations to identify and investigate loss/gain differences for each operation.
Monitor and advise the deals desk of all costs related to each transaction, maintaining P&L awareness.
Ensure operations are optimised to best commercial advantage, meeting all contractual obligations (e.g. minimising demurrage exposure).
Maximise recoveries; document, present and secure payment of all claims to third parties.
Maintain strong working relationships with trade support divisions — claims, deals desk, trade finance and chartering — and with counterparts and third-party service providers.
Train and develop less experienced members of the operations team to increase knowledge and commercial awareness.
Follow internal procedures and company policies; adhere to Trafigura's Code of Conduct, HSEC Policy and Business Principles.
Identify operational issues and escalate to the Regional Manager as appropriate.

Required qualifications
At least 5 years' experience in cargo operations in a global oil trading company.
Experience working on Gasoline cargo operations with a preference for experience with blending operations.
Ability to interpret the operational requirements of contracts and comment on operational aspects; understanding of the basic legal framework supporting oil contracts.
Ability to interpret charter party terms against the interacting oil contract; good understanding of common ship operations and terminology.
Good understanding of relevant petroleum product specifications, analytical methods, laboratory precision and inspection procedures.

Experience across multiple product desks (Gasoline, Distillates and Fuel Oil).
Familiarity with Pluto or similar trade operations management systems.
Exposure to storage logistics and reconciliation processes.

Attributes for success
Strong decision-making ability — comfortable navigating ambiguity and complexity in a fast-moving trading environment.
Effective networker who builds and maintains relationships with counterparts, service providers and internal stakeholders.
Organised and detail-oriented, with strong planning and prioritisation skills.
Resourceful and commercially aware, with a proactive approach to problem-solving.

Department overview
The Oil Cargo Operations department is responsible for the efficient and effective management of the physical movement of oil and petroleum products. The team ensures commodities are transported from origin to destination, meeting all contractual obligations and regulatory requirements. The department works closely with Traders, Finance, Deals Desk (Risk and P&L) and Chartering to support the full trade lifecycle.

jobs.title: Growth Marketer – E-Commerce
jobs.description:
Growth Marketer – E\-Commerce  
Location: Sonnentalstrasse 21, 8600 Dübendorf  
Work model: Hybrid – 4 days in the office  
Who we are  
Pflegewegweiser, part of the Entyre Group, is one of the fastest\-growing health\-tech scale\-ups in Switzerland and the US — 500\+ employees, locations from Zurich to Boston, and a mission that truly matters: helping people live independently at home. We make sure families are compensated for caring for their loved ones, and supply them with the homecare products they rely on every day.  
Pflegewegweiser Shop is a startup within this scale\-up. We're building an e\-commerce business from the ground up. That means: no legacy accounts to inherit, no 40\-page media plans, and no waiting three quarters for your test to go live. You launch it, you own it, you read and interpret the numbers, and you act accordingly.  
What you'll own  
The paid engine. You own Google Search, Shopping, and PMax end\-to\-end — from campaigns to assets to budget. You run the Merchant Center and the shopping feed like they're yours — because they are: clean data, healthy diagnostics, well\-maintained feeds.  
Meta \& creatives. You plan, launch, and optimize our Meta campaigns. You drive the creatives that feed them — static and video — from in\-house production to briefing and directing agencies. You know a winning ad isn't luck, it's a testing pipeline.  
Funnels. You build marketing funnels across the entire customer journey and continuously optimize them — from first click to repeat purchase.  
Growth sprints. You design experiments that open up new growth opportunities beyond day\-to\-day optimization. You find the growth opportunities we haven't identified or tapped yet.  
New bets. You develop new business models together with the Head of E\-Commerce, stress\-test them, and make them better — expanding what the shop can be.  
The setup. You question existing setups and processes, iterate on them, and make them better. If something is slow, manual, or "just grew that way," you challenge it.  
The shop. You help improve the shop experience, drive e\-commerce sales, and elevate the customer experience — your insights and improvement suggestions can be implemented quickly and directly to give our customers a better experience.  
The numbers. You analyze marketing and sales KPIs to find growth opportunities and efficiencies. Your analysis doesn't just go into a report — it directly influences our spending and budget allocations.  
What you bring  
2–5 years of marketing experience, preferably at a startup, scale\-up, or agency  
Hands\-on experience with paid campaigns on Google Ads and Meta — you've set up and optimized campaigns yourself, not just watched a dashboard  
A data\-driven understanding of marketing and e\-commerce KPIs — comfortable with reporting and able to move quickly from raw data to an actionable recommendation  
Ownership from day one — you'd rather build the process than wait for one  
Comfort with ambiguity and a healthy balance between speed and quality  
German and English \- both C1\+  
Nice to have  
Experience with Google Merchant Center and shopping feeds  
Familiarity with Shopify or a comparable e\-commerce platform  
Basic creative skills (Canva, CapCut, Figma, video production) and experience briefing creative agencies  
Knowledge of A/B testing, CRO, and funnel analytics  
An affinity for healthcare/homecare — or the curiosity to dive deep  
Why this role  
0 to 1, for real. You build the growth engine instead of waiting for someone else to.  
Direct line to leadership. You report to the Senior Growth Manager and work closely with the Chief Business Development Officer. Short paths, fast decisions, no bureaucracy. You learn fast, get direct feedback, and quickly gain ownership of your own topics and areas of responsibility.  
Impact you can see. Small, independent team; your tests land in the business immediately.  
Scale at your back. The pace and autonomy of a startup, backed by the resources of an international group — in one of the biggest growth markets there is: homecare and digital health.  
How we operate — non\-negotiable:  
"Insanely great" for families — delivered now  
Forget mere "satisfaction." We deliver support that makes caregivers feel seen, understood, and valued. Anticipate their needs and solve problems quickly. The standard is "insanely great," period. Anything less slows us down and fails our families.  
Speed is king — ruthless focus is key  
Velocity comes from focus. Eliminate distractions. Concentrate all effort on the \#1 critical objective until it's done, then move to the next. Decide what not to do and cut it ruthlessly. Being a mile wide and an inch deep is failure — move the needle now.  
Raise the bar — crush mediocrity  
Mediocrity kills speed, morale, and companies. Hunt it down and eliminate it. Good enough is never good enough. Demand top performance from yourself and everyone around you. Own your work, deliver excellence fast, and accept no excuses.  
The speed algorithm — question, delete, simplify, accelerate  
Build momentum by questioning every requirement: who asked, and why? Delete ruthlessly — parts, processes, bureaucracy. Simplify what remains. Accelerate cycle times relentlessly. "It can't be done" means "you haven't figured it out yet — go do it." Break bottlenecks, find shortcuts, remove friction.  
Act like owners — bold bets, fast action  
This is your company. Own the mission and the results. Take initiative, make bold bets that leapfrog progress, and act decisively. If you stumble, learn faster and go again. Bias for action is everything.  
The bottom line:  
We are building something vital at lightning speed. This requires intensity, focus, and a relentless drive to execute. If reading this makes you want to jump in and build faster, welcome to Pflegewegweiser!  
\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

jobs.description:
Replit is the agentic software creation platform that enables anyone to build applications using natural language. With millions of users worldwide, Replit is democratizing software development by removing traditional barriers to application creation.


Role Summary

Replit is the agentic software creation platform that enables anyone to build applications using natural language. With millions of users worldwide, Replit is democratizing software development by removing traditional barriers to application creation.

As a Disputes and Chargeback Program Manager at Replit, you’ll be part of our Trust and Safety Operations team, who owns customer-facing workflows that handle sensitive and policy-driven interactions across the Support organization. This includes areas such as privacy requests, DMCA and intellectual property claims, law enforcement requests, and abuse appeals.

You'll own Replit's disputes and chargeback function end-to-end: from the individual case in front of you to the policies, playbooks, and automation that let it hold up as we scale to millions of users. This role combines strategic ownership with hands-on execution: you'll determine dispute and chargeback strategy, and build the systems that make those decisions repeatable at scale, working closely with Engineering, Legal and Finance.

 

In this role you will…

 - Own the full dispute lifecycle: investigate incoming chargebacks and disputes, decide whether and how to represent, gather evidence, and respond within network deadlines.

 - Design and maintain the policies, decision trees, and SOPs that govern how disputes and chargebacks are handled.

 - Define the key metrics, health targets, and goals for the disputes program and track performance against them, reporting to leadership.

 - Monitor chargeback rates and dispute trends to identify the underlying drivers of volume, and partner with Engineering and Finance to address root causes.

 - Partner with Engineering and Support Operations to automate manual parts of the workflow (evidence gathering, decisioning logic, etc).

 - Build training, documentation, and escalation paths that enable frontline support teams to handle dispute-related inquiries confidently and consistently as the program scales.



Required Skills and Experience:

 - 6+ years of hands-on experience owning disputes/chargebacks operations, ideally where you built or significantly leveled up the function rather than just running an existing one.

 - Deep familiarity with major card network dispute rules and reason codes (e.g., Visa, Mastercard, Amex, Discover), including compelling-evidence frameworks and network monitoring/excessive-dispute programs (e.g., Visa's VDMP/VFMP, Mastercard's ECP)

 - Experience building or improving SOPs, playbooks, or workflows in a support or operations environment.

 - Experience partnering with Engineering to scope and prioritize automation, even if you're not writing the code yourself.

 - Comfort operating as both a hands-on operator and systems builder in a scaling environment.

 - Strong judgment and decision-making skills when handling sensitive or ambiguous customer situations.

 - Experience translating policy or legal requirements into clear, repeatable processes or customer-facing guidance.

 - Strong written communication skills, with the ability to communicate clearly, empathetically, and precisely in high-stakes situations.

 - Proven track record working cross-functionally to deliver impactful results.

 

Nice to Have:

 - Hands-on experience with Stripe's dispute tooling specifically, including submitting evidence and managing dispute workflows through Stripe.

 - Experience in customer support, trust & safety, support operations, or similar roles within a technology company.

 - Experience in a high-growth or usage-based SaaS environment, where dispute patterns and volume can shift quickly with product changes.

 - Familiarity with fraud detection tooling and how it intersects with the disputes function.

 - Experience managing outsourced or contract support as programs scale, in case this function grows beyond a single person down the line.

jobs.title: Senior/Media Manager
jobs.description:
Replit is the agentic software creation platform that enables anyone to build applications using natural language. With millions of users worldwide, Replit is democratizing software development by removing traditional barriers to application creation.



ABOUT THE ROLE

Replit is investing seriously in paid media — TV, CTV, online video, out-of-home, audio, social, and search — and we need the person who makes that investment work. This role is the internal owner of our media program: you'll direct our external media agencies, pressure-test their plans, steward the budget, and hold every dollar accountable for reaching the right audiences on the right channels at the right time.

You'll report to the VP of Marketing and act as the connective tissue between our brand and growth teams and our agency partners. This is not a hands-on-keyboard activation role. You won't be living in Ads Manager — you'll be the person who briefs the agency, challenges the channel mix, catches the pacing problem before it becomes a budget problem, and translates campaign performance into decisions leadership can act on.

This is the right role if you've sat on the brand side (or want to move there from a media agency), you know what a great media plan looks like and what a lazy one looks like, and you get energy from being the sharpest media mind in the room without needing to touch the platforms yourself.



WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Agency leadership: Serve as the primary day-to-day partner to our media agencies. Set strategy direction, write clear briefs, run planning cycles and QBRs, and hold partners accountable for performance, optimization, quality, and business results.

 - Plan interrogation: Review and challenge agency recommendations across every channel — TV, CTV, OLV, OOH, audio, social, search, programmatic. Catch weak rationale, frequency saturation risks, and budget misallocations before plans get approved.

 - Budget stewardship: Own media budget pacing, forecasting, authorizations, and reconciliation in partnership with Finance. Monitor spend and delivery mid-flight, flag risks early, and drive reallocations when the data says to.

 - Media strategy & planning: Lead annual, quarterly, and campaign-level planning with the agency. Make sure plans reflect our audiences, product moments, competitive pressure, and business goals — not just what's easy to buy.

 - Measurement & accountability: Define campaign KPIs and measurement frameworks with the agency and our analytics team. Own wrap reports, drive a test-and-learn agenda (incrementality, brand lift, MMM as we scale), and go beyond CPMs and impressions to reach efficiency and cost-per-outcome.

 - Executive reporting: Distill campaign and channel performance into clear recommendations for marketing leadership. Tell us what worked, what didn't, and what we should do differently — with numbers behind it.

 - Cross-functional alignment: Partner with Brand, Growth, Creative, Product Marketing, Social, and Comms so media plans amplify what the rest of marketing is building, and so creative assets fit the placements we're buying.



REQUIRED SKILLS & EXPERIENCE

 - 5+ years of media planning and strategy experience, either brand-side managing external agencies or at a media agency serving major consumer brands

 - Demonstrated experience independently reviewing and challenging agency media plans, not just executing against them

 - Experience managing multi-million dollar media budgets across concurrent campaigns, including pacing, forecasting, and mid-flight reallocation

 - Fluency across the full channel landscape: TV/CTV, online video, OOH, audio/podcasts, paid social, search, and programmatic — you can evaluate rates, rationale, and audience fit in any of them

 - Strong command of media measurement: reach and frequency, brand lift, incrementality testing, and marketing mix modeling

 - Sharp analytical skills; you can work from raw campaign data to find performance trends and budget inefficiencies, and you're at home in Excel

 - Strong stakeholder management across Finance, Analytics, Creative, and agency teams; you write briefs people can actually work from

 - AI-native: actively using AI tools to speed up analysis, reporting, and planning work — you're not just aware of them, you're using them daily

 - Comfort operating in ambiguity and at speed; you don't need committee consensus to make smart decisions



BONUS QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience at a high-growth consumer tech, B2C, or AI company

 - Agency alumni who've made (or want to make) the move to the client side

 - Experience standing up a media function or measurement framework from scratch

 - Experience with OOH and large cultural-moment buys (sponsorships, tentpole events)

 - A point of view on how AI is changing media planning and buying — and what most brands get wrong about it

 - Active Replit user; you've built and shipped something with the product

 - Based in or able to relocate to the San Francisco Bay Area

jobs.title: Go-to-Market Responsible
jobs.description:
Do you enjoy turning product direction into commercially successful go-to-market plans? Are you motivated by bringing collections to life across retail, e-commerce and other consumer-facing channels? And do you thrive in the role that connects Product, Brand Identity and commercial execution?

Then you may be the Go-to-Market Responsible we are looking for.

YOUR TEAM
You'll join our E-Commerce & DTC Marketing team, where we bring our collections to market across retail, e-commerce and other consumer-facing channels. As our GTM Responsible, you'll work closely with specialists across CRM, Media, Retail & E-Commerce while partnering with Product, Brand Identity and B2B Communications to ensure every launch is successfully planned and delivered.

YOUR ROLE
As our Go-to-Market Responsible, you'll own the annual DTC go-to-market plan, translating product direction into commercially successful market launches. Working closely with Product, Brand Identity and key business stakeholders, you'll shape go-to-market plans that connect product direction with commercial execution across retail, e-commerce and other consumer-facing channels.
You'll ensure product direction is translated into clear plans, strong cross-functional collaboration and successful execution, bringing launches to market on time and supporting both revenue growth and brand awareness.

Your key responsibilities include:

  • Developing and driving the annual DTC go-to-market plan

  • Translating product direction into campaign and rollout plans

  • Planning and coordinating market launches across retail, e-commerce and other consumer-facing channels

  • Driving timelines and cross-functional execution from planning to launch

  • Coordinating stakeholders across Product, Brand Identity and B2B Communications

  • Using commercial performance and brand insights to optimize future go-to-market planning.

YOUR BENEFITS

jobs.title: Senior Lead Project Manager for IT Technology project
jobs.description:
Are you a very experienced Project Manager with a passion for driving big and complex projects involving software development together with a big global vendor? Do you enjoy leading highly skilled teams in a dynamic and international environment? Then you may be our new Senior Lead Project Manager.

Nordic RCC – supporting security of supply and the green energy transition

Nordic Regional Coordination Centre (RCC) provides critical services and insights to support the national Transmission System Operators (TSOs) in Finland, Norway, Sweden and Denmark — to ensure the efficient operation and use of the Nordic power system and high security of power supply at any time. Join Nordic RCC and contribute to ensuring a secure and sustainable energy in the future.

Job description

Nordic RCC seeks a skilled and experienced Project Manager to drive an IT project with many internal and external stakeholders, several deliverables and milestones, delivered within agreed go-live dates.

You will be responsible for coordinating all aspects of the project as scoping, planning, execution and delivery. Working closely together with a big global vendor and senior stakeholders across Nordic RCC, you will ensure seamless collaboration and a transparent strong approach to project management.

You will guide the project team incl. project managers through strong project risk management and planning, dependencies to other projects, financial control, stakeholder alignment, and progress monitoring in close collaboration with the internal and external Steercos, ensuring alignment with Nordic RCC’s goals.

Your primary tasks and areas of responsibility:

  • Facilitate a strong collaboration and communication among program/project stakeholders from the different departments in the organization, the vendor's project organisation and the internal/external Steercos

  • In control of budget, forecast and monthly financial updates, incl. alignment with financial milestones from vendor

  • In control of project scope, resource needs according to project plan, manage project risks continuously through the project lifetime in close collaboration with vendor, internal project managers and the Steercos

  • In control of develop, coordinate, communicate and execute project plans with clear milestones and deadlines, ensuring to deliver all milestones on time in close collaboration with both vendor and Nordic RCC

  • Monitor program/project progress, assess performance, and report outcomes to key stakeholders/Steercos by monthly meetings and reporting to Leadership team in Nordic RCC

  • Lead a strong transition from each go-live to operational phase, ensuring an organized handover to line organization for the different deliverables

  • Use best practices and processes, e.g. Stage Gate Model, Governance model, Resource management, Project Risk Management etc. to provide the optimal guidance to cross-functional project teams throughout the project lifecycle with focus on balancing quality, efficiency, deliver on time and financials

Required skills and experience

The ideal candidate holds a BA or MA in IT with strong project or program management experience working with software development in an IT project in collaboration with a big global vendor.

Key skills include:

  • Strong drive and passion for project management, ensuring the project teams deliver on time in expected quality/scope and in control of finance

  • Strong organizational, planning and time management skills

  • Proven track record in managing senior stakeholder expectations and leading cross-functional teams in collaboration with an IT vendor

  • Experience in communicating both big-picture objectives and project details, ensuring all project managers/team members understand their roles and contributions

  • Demonstrated ability to identify challenges early and proactively drive deliverables in collaboration with vendor and project teams

  • At least 10 years of relevant experience in IT project management with a global vendor

  • Relevant project management certificates and e.g., relevant change management certificates

  • Full professional proficiency in English

Employment conditions

You will join a company of competent, diverse, and enthusiastic colleagues. We are currently more than 24 nationalities with more than 30% women (striving to improve this balance) and all ages.

 Your daily workplace will be in our newly furnished office premises in Copenhagen Towers, Ørestad. We are offering workplace flexibility to ensure a healthy work-life balance including the possibility for working from home some of your worktime. 

Our values of fellowship, curiosity, respect, and transparency have been defined by all employees. They identify how we behave and shape the way we work together, and we expect you to see yourself in them.

The position is conditioned upon a satisfactory background check as well as a national security clearance, both of which will be facilitated by Nordic RCC. You can read more on security clearance here. Please also note, that the process includes that any spouse, registered partner, cohabitant, steady partner, co-resident, child over 18 living at home and parent with the same address as the candidate must also consent to be examined. 

Application deadline and contact information

Please apply online as soon as possible (in English) on https://www.globesearch.dk/jobs/8221470 . We may conduct interviews on a continuous basis.

A cover letter is not required, but we kindly ask you to include a few sentences in your CV explaining why you are interested in the position. Applications are only accepted through our online recruitment system. 

To ensure a fair and unbiased recruitment process, we kindly request that you do not include photographs in your CVs or application materials.

jobs.title: Research Assistant in Regenerative Medicine
jobs.description:
A position as a full-time research assistant is vacant in the lab of Dr. Srustidhar Das, at the Department of Clinical Research and at the Research Unit of Inflammation Research, Department of Molecular Medicine, Faculty of Health Sciences, University of Southern Denmark. 

The position is limited to one year with the possibility of extension and/or continuing further as a PhD student, subject to funding and fulfilment of SDU's PhD admission requirements.

Job description

The position primarily consists of research within tissue regeneration, epithelial biology and inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), with limited research-based teaching or supervision activities where relevant. The research assistant will join a translational research programme that aims to understand how inflammation reshapes the intestinal epithelium and its surrounding tissue niche, and how these changes can be therapeutically targeted to restore safe and durable mucosal healing.

The position will suit a highly motivated candidate with a strong interest in mucosal biology, epithelial regeneration, organoid models, immune-stromal-epithelial interactions, single-cell and spatial technologies, and clinically oriented biomedical research. The successful candidate will work at the interface of experimental biology, translational medicine and omics-based research.

Research environment

The research assistant will be embedded in a dynamic and highly collaborative research environment spanning the Institute for Molecular Medicine and the Department of Clinical Research at SDU. The project benefits from close interactions among basic scientists, clinicians, bioinformaticians and translational researchers, with strong links to Odense University Hospital and access to patient-derived material, advanced disease models and state-of-the-art molecular technologies.

The environment provides excellent opportunities to develop practical and analytical skills in experimental and translational biomedicine, contribute to clinically relevant discoveries in IBD and tissue regeneration, and prepare for a potential subsequent PhD project.

Research project

The project investigates how prior inflammation leaves a lasting memory in the intestinal epithelium and its surrounding tissue niche, and how this memory affects mucosal healing in IBD. The research assistant will help establish and apply experimental models based on patient-derived intestinal biopsies, organoids, fibroblasts and immune-cell co-cultures to study epithelial regeneration in health and disease.

The work will also support the generation and functional validation of findings from single-cell and spatial approaches, including single-cell RNA sequencing, single-cell chromatin accessibility analysis, spatial transcriptomics and spatial epigenomics. Depending on experience and project needs, the research assistant may contribute to CRISPR-based genetic engineering of patient-derived organoids.

Key responsibilities

  • Establish, maintain and experimentally manipulate patient-derived intestinal organoids and relevant co-culture systems involving fibroblasts and immune cells.

  • Design and perform functional assays to assess epithelial regeneration, inflammatory responses, barrier function and cell-state plasticity.

  • Apply molecular and cellular methods such as qPCR, immunostaining, microscopy, flow cytometry, ELISA-based assays and related techniques.

  • Support sample preparation and experimental workflows for single-cell and spatial transcriptomic or epigenomic studies.

  • Contribute to CRISPR-based genetic engineering and functional validation of candidate pathways, depending on prior experience.

  • Work with patient-derived material in close collaboration with clinicians, bioinformaticians and translational researchers.

  • Maintain accurate experimental records, analyse and document results, and contribute to protocol development and optimisation.

  • Present results at group meetings and contribute to scientific reports, manuscripts, conferences, teaching and collaborative activities where relevant.

Expectations of qualifications 

The applicant is expected to hold a relevant master's degree or equivalent qualification in molecular biology, biomedicine, immunology, cell biology, biotechnology, medicine, bioinformatics or a closely related discipline.

Essential qualifications

  • A strong interest in mucosal biology, tissue regeneration, epithelial biology, inflammatory disease and translational biomedical research.

  • Hands-on experience with mammalian cell culture, molecular biology, primary cells, organoids, immunology, epithelial biology, inflammation research or related experimental systems.

  • Strong written and spoken English communication skills.

  • A structured, curious and technically careful working style, with the ability to work independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team.

  • Good organisational skills and a commitment to reproducible research, careful documentation and responsible handling of research data and biological material.

Desirable qualifications

  • Experience with intestinal organoids, patient-derived material, immune-cell culture, fibroblast culture or epithelial-stromal-immune co-culture models.

  • Familiarity with qPCR, immunostaining, confocal or advanced microscopy, flow cytometry, ELISA or MSD assays, and CRISPR-based genetic engineering.

  • Experience with, or a strong interest in learning, single-cell RNA sequencing, ATAC-seq, spatial transcriptomics, spatial epigenomics or computational analysis of omics datasets.

  • Interest in developing and optimising experimental models that connect mechanistic biology with clinically relevant questions in IBD and mucosal healing.

  • Previous experience with bioinformatics, statistics or image analysis will be considered an advantage but is not essential.

Research strategy for OUH and the Department of Clinical Research

The joint research strategy for the Department of Clinical Research and Odense University Hospital sets the direction for our shared research efforts in the years ahead. Rooted in the vision –We conduct research together to shape the patient care of the future – it focuses in particular on: cross-disciplinary research – with people at the centre; strong research environments – as drivers of development; and the research journey – from idea to impact. Further information on the joint research strategy of the Department of Clinical Research and Odense University Hospital is available here.

Further information 

For further information please contact 

Srustidhar Das
Department of Clinical Research and Department of Molecular Medicine
University of Southern Denmark (SDU)
Tel.: +45 71504339
E-mail: srudas@health.sdu.dk

Application deadline

September 15, 2026, at 23.59 hrs. (CET/CEST).

Salary and terms of employment

The applicant will be employed in accordance with the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and AC (the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations). 

The position as research assistant is placed within salary steps 4–8 of the Danish state salary scale, depending on seniority. In addition, a centrally agreed research assistant allowance is paid, and further qualification- and function-related allowances may be negotiated. 

The work location will be at Campusvej 55, 5230 Odense M.   

Application

Applications must be submitted electronically using the link “Apply now” - see below.

We strongly recommend that you read How to apply for a position at SDU before you apply.

Only applications written in English will be accepted for evaluation.

The application must include (as PDF files) (please note that the application (the motivation letter) and CV must not exceed 10 MB in total):

  • a motivation letter

  • a detailed CV

  • degree certificates (inclusive of master’s degree)

  • an explanation of other qualifications relevant to the position

For technical issues, please contact: hcm-support@sdu.dk

Please note that all the above-mentioned information must be included in the application.  

Applications received after the deadline and/or incomplete applications will not be considered.

Assessment

Shortlisting will be used as part of the initial selection process. 

Assessment of shortlisted applications will be done under the existing Appointment Order for universities. Shortlisted applications will be assessed by an assessment committee. The committee may request additional information, and, if so, it is the responsibility of the applicant to provide the necessary material. 

When the assessment committee has submitted its report, the applicants will receive part of the evaluation that concerns themselves. 

References will be obtained for the preferred candidate from their current and previous employers. Applicants invited for interview should expect to complete a work-related personality assessment.

Living and working in Denmark

Foreign applicants will be offered Danish language training as part of the employment. 

The International Staff Office (ISO) at SDU provides a variety of services for new employees, guests and people who consider applying for a job at the University of Southern Denmark. 

The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

jobs.description:
WHO WE ARE

Notion is the collaborative AI workspace where teams and agents think together https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vkpYpWfEK5s. We're building one place where your knowledge, projects, meetings, and AI tools live side by side, so work is faster, clearer, and less fragmented. Millions of individuals, small teams, and large companies run their work on Notion.



Notinos (our employees) are customer zero in bringing this future of work to life. We care about craft, building things that last, and the belief that great work is still fundamentally human. Our goal isn’t to ship the next feature. Each and every team of Notinos is working to set the standard for how humans work together in the AI era. From building a business’s system of record to making and managing AI agents to automating away the busy work, we care deeply about giving our customers more time for their life’s work.




ABOUT THE ROLE:

We're looking for a Head of Enterprise Segment, Japan to lead Notion's Enterprise GTM motion in Japan as we evolve how we sell, build, and deliver outcomes for our largest customers. This is a senior second-line leadership role, leading leaders and teams across the Enterprise segment, with accountability for new logo acquisition, expansion, renewals, and the quality of execution that produces durable customer outcomes.

This person will play an integral role in scaling Notion's evolving GTM motion in Japan. You'll help define what great looks like for the Enterprise segment: how teams identify the right accounts, create urgency with executives, diagnose workflows, run compelling first and second meetings, deliver live builds and value narratives, and hand customers off into adoption with clarity. This is not a traditional pipeline-management role. The best leaders in this motion are coaches first: they can inspect the quality of a customer conversation, watch a live build or deal review, and tell a manager or IC exactly what to change.

As part of the Japan GTM leadership team, you'll be instrumental in helping define our Enterprise sales motion, meaningfully shape our product and customer strategy, and drive revenue growth while building a high-performing team. We need someone with an entrepreneurial and builder spirit, strong enterprise operating discipline, and experience leading through managers. This person should enjoy coaching leaders and reps to be the best they can be, be data-driven, and be experienced in managing complex, high-velocity Enterprise pipeline across new business, expansion, and renewal motions.




WHAT YOU'LL ACHIEVE:

 - Lead the Japan Enterprise Segment strategy, including territory design, account prioritization, pipeline generation, executive engagement, expansion strategy, renewal health, and long-term revenue growth

 - Lead and develop first-line leaders and senior ICs across the Enterprise motion, raising the bar on coaching quality, operating cadence, performance management, and team execution

 - Own the commercial performance of the Enterprise segment across new logo ARR, expansion ARR, renewals, and UBP outcomes, accountable for both the headline numbers and the quality of execution that drives them

 - Scale the evolved GTM motion in-market, including account strategy, workflow diagnosis, current → future architecture, live builds in Notion, value narratives, mutual action plans, and adoption hand-offs

 - Build the operating rhythm and inspection cadence for the segment, including weekly pipeline reviews, deal support sessions, call reviews against the motion quality rubric, forecast calls, and leadership reporting

 - Partner with Solutions Consultants and Outcomes Architects (Sales and Customer Success), BDR, Partnerships, Marketing, Deal Desk, Ops, Legal, and Product to build playbooks and define how Notion wins with Enterprise customers in Japan

 - Partner with BDR leadership on Enterprise pipeline strategy, outbound targeting, qualification standards, and messaging so the team's book of business is healthy and growing

 - Partner with Solutions Consultant and Outcomes Architect leadership on adoption hand-offs, at-risk account management, and renewal strategy, owning the overall commercial arc while collaborating on execution after close

 - Represent Japan Enterprise customer and team signal in regional and global leadership forums, clearly identifying what's working, what needs investment, and where execution is breaking down

 - Attract, hire, onboard, certify, and retain a world-class Enterprise organization, building a culture of high performance, coaching, accountability, and collaboration




SKILLS YOU'LL NEED TO BRING:

 - 10+ years of B2B SaaS, AI, productivity, collaboration, or workflow technology experience, with a proven track record of winning and growing Enterprise customers

 - 3+ years of second-line leadership experience, with experience leading managers or multiple teams through a defined operating cadence, performance management, and talent development rhythm

 - Strong understanding of PLG and SLG sales motions, with successful experience combining bottom-up adoption with top-down executive selling in Enterprise accounts

 - Proven ability to scale a GTM transformation or new sales motion, including enablement, inspection, manager coaching, playbook adoption, and consistent execution across teams

 - Strong enterprise customer instincts, with the ability to guide teams through complex discovery, multi-stakeholder evaluation, technical validation, business case creation, and adoption planning

 - Deep coaching orientation: you can inspect a deal review, customer call, or live build and identify specifically what needs to change, not just whether the outcome was good

 - Strong analytical judgment, able to read pipeline health, identify risk early, use customer and team signal to build strategy, and drive urgency without micromanaging

 - Excellent cross-functional leadership skills, with experience partnering across Sales, Customer Success, Product, Marketing, Partnerships, Operations, Legal, and Deal Desk

 - A builder mentality who thrives in collaborative environments, operates well in ambiguity, and creates structure, playbooks, and operating rhythms where they do not yet exist

 - Executive presence and communication skills, with the ability to engage senior customer stakeholders and represent Japan Enterprise priorities to regional and global leadership

 - Fluency in Japanese (native or bilingual level) and English (high-business level)

 - You don't need to be an AI expert, but you're curious and willing to adopt AI tools to work smarter, coach better, and deliver stronger customer outcomes.




NICE TO HAVES:

 - Experience leading Enterprise GTM in Japan or across APAC for a high-growth SaaS or AI company

 - Experience leading through a major GTM organizational change, sales methodology rollout, segment redesign, or role redesign across Enterprise teams

 - Experience selling or leading teams in a consumption, usage-based, or adoption-led business where customer outcomes matter as much as closed ARR

 - Track record building high-performing regional teams from an early stage, including hiring to profile, structured onboarding, certification, and performance management

 - Strong technical fluency or experience working closely with technical sales, solutions consulting, product, implementation, or partner teams

 - Experience selling through or partnering with systems integrators, channel partners, or strategic alliances in Japan

 - Experience with quarterly or annual sales planning, territory planning, and Enterprise capacity planning




A NOTE ON AI

You don’t need deep AI expertise for every role, but we do expect every Notino to be intellectually curious, drawn to tinkering and discovery, and excited to use AI as a real collaborator in their work. For some roles, AI fluency is a core requirement — when that’s the case, we'll say so explicitly in the qualifications. People who thrive here don’t treat AI as a novelty. They use it to think better, and make their work easier for others to build on.

At EY, we're all in to shape your future with confidence.  
We'll help you succeed in a globally connected powerhouse of diverse teams and take your career wherever you want it to go.  
Join EY and help to build a better working world.  
Senior Consultant \- Assurance \- Technology Risk  
The opportunity  
Our Consulting business offers a broad range of functional and cross\-country services dedicated to providing high\-value and trusted advice to clients, with a specific focus on business transformation programs.  
Your key responsibilities  
You will gain insights into cutting\-edge IT environments and into our global methodology. Your focus: analysis, evaluation and optimization of processes, structures and systems  
As a member of interdisciplinary specialist teams, you will audit operational IT systems and information portals with regard to internal control and risk and compliance management. This includes migration tests, third party attestation \& certification, IT risk assessments, information security assessments and data analytics/information management  
You will learn about "thought leadership" as a way of addressing today's constantly changing market and challenges. You will expand your expertise with every project alongside our leaders. Furthermore, you will be supported with trainings, courses and learnings in relevant fields  
Skills and attributes for success  
Degree (Bachelor or Master) in Economics or (Business\-) Information Technology is required, relevant certifications (e.g. CISA, CISSP, CISM or CRISC) are an advantage  
A must: 3\-4 years' experience in carrying out IT audits (e.g. at a Big4 company or internal audit department) or in the area of IT risk management / operational risk management, preferably at an international company  
Qualities guaranteed to boost your career at EY: ability to work in a team, determination, commitment and quick comprehension. As a Swiss international company, we require German and English  
What we offer you  
At EY, we'll develop you with future\-focused skills and equip you with world\-class experiences. We'll empower you in a flexible environment, and fuel you and your extraordinary talents in a diverse and inclusive culture of globally connected teams. Learn more.  
Click here to find out more about our benefits and corporate social responsibility.

jobs.description:
We are a world leading Engine MRO service provider, headquartered in Zurich, Switzerland, with over 90 years of operational experience. Our unwavering dedication to innovation, excellence and environmental responsibility propels us forward on our journey to becoming the leading, most customer-centric, and sustainable Engine focused MRO worldwide.

Working with an extensive network of partners and business development offices in Europe, the USA, Asia and the Middle East, we offer comprehensive, fully customized solutions for the Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul of aircraft engines, airframes and components sales business including impeccable technical support to over 500 customers worldwide. Our mission: We safely power your flight.

We are looking for dedicated and skilled individuals to join our shop floor across several areas and departments at Zurich-Airport. If this sounds appealing to you, we encourage you to apply for our Supervisor position.

You will coordinate the team’s work with its direct stakeholders at SR Technics to the goals and missions of the organization.

Supervisor Engine Shop Floor 100%

- Promote a positive Safety Culture and ensure that Safety and Quality Policy are communicated/promoted and implemented within the Organization.
- Lead and manage a multi-cultural team, fostering performance, engagement, and a positive work environment.
- Drive performance culture through periodic target setting and regular structured follow up with all employees. Apply performance management process (PMP) and leadership with a focus on employee motivation.
- Plan and allocate resources to ensure high productivity and monitor labor efficiency
- Drive personnel development and skill management to meet capacity requirements (OJT, qualifications, certifications, performance evaluations).
- Execute and promote Continuous Improvements in applying Lean principles and 5S to achieve the organization targets and key performance indicators (KPI).
- Participate in, prepare for and be responsible for internal and external audits

Your Profile

- Technical background or technical education (aviation experience is a plus)
- Leadership experience with strong interpersonal skills and leadership skills with the ability to lead, motivate, and develop teams. Minimum 3 years team leadership or strong project leadership preferred.
- Excellent communication, leadership, and problem-solving skills in a fast-paced environment and strong focus on safety, quality, and cost efficiency
- Proactive, independent, and self-initiated working style with high performance drive
- Knowledge and experience in applying Lean/Six Sigma methodology
- Proficient in English (B2+), German is an advantage
- Proficiency with maintenance documentation systems. Microsoft Office required, SAP is an advantage
